description: The same job, installing the small tree program, checking it and removing it again, with the package tools of Debian, Fedora, AlmaLinux, openSUSE and Alpine.
environment: Each host ran in a Docker container on Docker Desktop (arm64), so the kernel is Docker Desktop's (Linux 7.0.14-linuxkit), not the distribution's.
On the Debian hosts, systemd runs as PID 1, as on a real machine.
The hosts share a network in documentation address ranges (192.0.2.0/24 and 2001:db8:1::/64, gateway 192.0.2.1). A dnsmasq container at 192.0.2.53 answers for tuxpixel.example.
Commands ran in a login shell on an 80-column terminal, with the pagers of systemd and dpkg turned off (SYSTEMD_PAGER=cat, DPKG_PAGER=cat).
Sockets on 127.0.0.11 belong to Docker's built-in DNS service, which every container on such a network has.
nginx is set to start 2 worker processes rather than one per CPU, to keep process listings short.
Each distribution ran in its official container image, logged in as root, with the package lists as the image ships them (Debian empties them, so apt update runs first).
